messages:
priya: hey team - trying to trace down request logs for req_id=req_4f8b2a7e. I can see trace trace-ab12 in the console but clicking spans just shows service/latency, no direct log links. where's the fastest place to grab the raw request+response payload?

matt: if you have the trace open, click a top-level span -> 'Related logs' should populate, but sometimes the span doesn't surface the x-request-id header. Did the trace originate at the edge/nginx proxy or an internal service?

priya: edge proxy at ingress-nginx -> then routed to gateway. trace shows a span on "edge-proxy" and a second on "gateway". the trace start span has attributes: http.request_id = req_4f8b2a7e

jack: CLI route: if you have gcloud logging access use:
`gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.http.request_id="req_4f8b2a7e"' --limit 200 --project=redwood-prod`
That returns structured logs with payload. If you prefer k8s-level tailing (quick when you know pod):
`stern -n prod "gateway" --since 1m | rg "req_4f8b2a7e" -n`
or
`kubectl logs -n prod <gateway-pod> -c gateway | rg "req_4f8b2a7e" -n`

zoe: FYI the edge proxy sometimes rewrites the header to x-request-ref. Check both keys in the trace attributes and search for either. Also check the ingress logs (namespace=kube-system or namespace=edge) — ingress pods often have the earliest request line.

matt: if the console trace has a span id you can map to a pod via span -> resource.attributes.k8s.pod.name. We have a tiny helper endpoint:
`https://observability.redwood.internal/trace-to-req?trace=trace-ab12`
It will return candidate request_ids and pod names (internal only). Observability-bot can also post a mapping.

observability-bot: mapping found for trace-ab12 -> req candidates: [req_4f8b2a7e], pods: [gateway-5f8b7d9c, edge-2a1b3c4d]. link: https://observability.redwood.internal/trace/trace-ab12 (internal)

jack: another trick: if console logs are sampled, try using raw logging backend (BigQuery/Cloud Logging) and query JSON fields. Example BigQuery SQL:
`SELECT timestamp, payload FROM 
`project.dataset.logs`
WHERE JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(payload, '$.http.request_id') = 'req_4f8b2a7e' LIMIT 100;`

priya: awesome — used the gcloud command and found the gateway pod logs with the full request body. saved. thanks! :thumbsup:

zoe: if you want a permanent quicklink, file an ops ticket and we can add a dashboard panel that accepts request_id and runs the gcloud query via a small script.

priya: will do. marking this resolved for now. thanks everyone!
